import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        mean_diff = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        effects.append((fid, abs(mean_diff), abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (mean difference) descending
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Filter out correlated features (|r| >= 0.6) to avoid redundancy
    selected_features = set()
    for fid, _, _, _ in effects:
        is_correlated = False
        for selected_fid in selected_features:
            col1 = feats.column(selected_fid)
            col2 = feats.column(fid)
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                is_correlated = True
                break
        if not is_correlated:
            selected_features.add(fid)
            if len(selected_features) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # Select top features based on effect size and statistical significance
    drivers = [fid for fid, _, _, p in effects if fid in selected_features and p < 0.1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # For products, look for strong pairwise interactions among top features
    products = []
    top_fids = set(drivers)
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(drivers):
        for fid2 in drivers[i+1:]:
            # Check if they're not too similar (correlation < 0.8)
            col1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col2 = feats.column(fid2)
            corr = abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1])
            if corr < 0.8:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Build loadings dictionary for weighted score
    loadings = {}
    for fid in selected_features:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by standardized effect size (t-statistic)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        y = feats.y
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        loadings[fid] = abs(t_stat)
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(selected_features),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
